order: Fix three cross-platform faults the first integration run found in the runner that ships to projects; none are test artifacts. First, restore the documented install on Windows: the runtime refuses to spawn .cmd and .bat files directly, and a package-manager install of the engine command resolves to a .cmd shim first, so route engine launches through the command interpreter with every argument quoted — not a bare shell option, which does not quote and would split the first path containing a space. Second, make the scratch-outside-the-repository guarantee hold where the repository path contains a symlink: every path comparison must resolve both sides, including paths that do not exist yet, by resolving the deepest existing ancestor and re-attaching the rest. Third, a configured scratch root must be validated before anything is created inside it, with the post-creation check kept as the backstop for roots the runner picks itself. Also have the probe distinguish a launch failure from a failed echo.
claims: All three are fixed in the runner: Windows engine launches go through the command interpreter with each argument quoted, every path comparison resolves both sides including paths that do not yet exist, and a configured scratch root is validated before anything is created in it. The probe now separates a launch failure from a failed echo. A regression test reproduces the symlink shape on every platform and asserts nothing was written into the repository, across 96 checks.
